record.body:
**Root cause: this module could never start a roll. It could only reskin one the engine already started.**

Both trigger paths required `engineCombatRoll` to already be true — the source comment says so outright: *"must already be true, so this can only ever split one true interval into two rolls, never invent a roll."*

Your installed session proves the engine never starts one on foot:

```
[roll] heartbeat stage=idle engineCombatRoll=0 pending=0 charged=0 dictLoaded=1 frames=4335
```

`dictLoaded=1` — the clips were streamed and ready the whole time. `engineCombatRoll=0` on every heartbeat. RDR2 does not perform a combat roll on foot, so the trigger condition was unreachable and the feature has never once fired. That is why this has stayed open.

**Fix:** added an initiation path. A dive press now starts the roll directly instead of waiting for a roll the game never performs — which is what "when you WOULD dive, you should do a dodge roll" actually asks for.

Guards, so this doesn't become a free move:
- `dodgeRollGateApplies()` already excludes vehicle, mount and swimming, so a real water dive is untouched.
- Requires the roll to be idle with no trigger pending, so a press mid-roll still falls through to the existing chained path instead of restarting.
- **Stamina still applies.** Initiation enters the same block that branches on `affordable`; an unaffordable press is refused and logged, not performed.

**Worth knowing:** this is the first build where the stamina gate is load-bearing. Until now the engine never rolled, so the gate could never be exercised — which is why your log shows `refusals=0` despite 989 suppressed frames. If unlimited rolling appears, the `GATE BYPASSED` line added for Lexer-Lux/Lexeditor#271 will name it.

Installed `28301C9D…`. Note the Lexer-Lux/Lexeditor#106 and Lexer-Lux/Lexeditor#271 verifiers cannot run — they read `_downloads/combat-roll-reference/extracted/CombatRoll.asi`, destroyed in the cleanup (see Lexer-Lux/Lexeditor#281). I did not weaken them to make them pass.
